# Plan: A viewer for documents — text, JSON, XML and logs

**Source**: free-form request (2026-08-16), revised after the logs-reuse note
**Backlog entry to write**: `docs/backlog.md` §3.25
**Complexity**: Large (new domain package + new view + three producers + one dependency),
but **net-negative in `internal/ui/containers`**, which loses its whole logs pane.

## Summary

A new view — `viewer` — displays a document read-only. A JSON or an XML document
opens on a **navigable tree**; either can be switched to its **own text**, with
syntax highlighting on or off. A **log** document opens as text with a verbosity
filter.

Three producers, one destination:

| Producer | Key | Document |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaces` | `enter` on a file | detected from the extension, then the content |
| `containers` | `i` | `docker inspect` — JSON |
| `containers` | `l` | `docker logs` — log |

That is the shape the security view already has (opened from workspaces *and*
from the OCI images list), and it is built the same way: the producer hands the
router one message, the router installs the view and records where `esc` returns.

## What this deletes

The containers view already owns a text pane — `stateLogs`, a `viewport`, soft
wrap, ANSI stripping, CR normalisation, scroll keys, reload, an external pager,
follow and a timestamps toggle. **None of it is containers-specific except the
last three**, and those are properties of *where the text came from*, not of the
pane. So the pane moves into the viewer and containers loses:

`viewState` · `stateLogs` · `logsViewport` · `logsContainerID` ·
`logsContainerName` · `logsLoading` · `logsRawContent` · `logsWrapEnabled` ·
`logsTimestamps` · `handleLogsKeyMsg` · `refreshLogsViewport` · `wrapLines` ·
`toggleLogsWrap` · `toggleLogsTimestamps` · `openExternalPager` ·
`followContainerLogs` · `handleContainerLogsLoaded` · `ContainerLogsLoadedMsg` ·
`inspectSelectedContainer`'s pager path · the `stateLogs` branches in
`InEditMode`, `GetFooterHeight`, `RenderFooter`, `GetShortcuts`, `View` and
`resize`.

`wrapLines` and the ANSI/CR normalisation are **moved**, not rewritten — they are
correct, and the reasons in their comments (systemd colours the output, progress
bars overwrite with `\r`) apply to any text this app displays, not just to logs.

`PagerExitMsg` stays: the shell path still uses it. Only its `stateLogs` branch
goes.

---

## Decisions taken

### Two display axes, not four names — **confirmed**

The request named *tree*, *raw*, *plain text* and a highlight toggle. Four names,
two independent facts:

| Axis | Values | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Display | `tree` or `text` | `f` |
| Highlight | on / off | `c` |

"Plain text" is `text` with colour off. A third display that additionally
discarded the detected format was put to the user and declined: it would make
`plain + colour on` and `text + colour off` two names for one screen. A document
with no structure (`.md`, `.go`, a log) is always `text`, and `f` is hidden for it
(Rule 130).

### chroma as a lexer, never as a formatter — **confirmed**

`github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2` (v2.27.0, pure Go, no cgo), chosen over ~250
hand-written lines of escape and CDATA handling, and the only route to Go, YAML
or Dockerfile later. It embeds every lexer, so the binary grows by a few MB —
the accepted cost, to be measured and recorded in §3.25.

`chroma/v2/formatters` is **never imported**. It writes its own ANSI colour and
reset sequences, and a reset inside a line strips the app background for
everything after it (Rule 115). Only `lexers.Get(...).Tokenise` is used; the
classes are mapped to theme styles by the UI package.

### A source, not a byte slice

The logs pane can reload, follow and re-fetch with timestamps. A viewer holding
only `[]byte` cannot do any of that, and neither could it reload a file the user
has just edited. So a document carries **where it came from**:

```go
type Source interface {
    Name() string                 // what the header shows
    Kind() Kind                   // declared by the producer, or KindAuto
    Load() ([]byte, error)
}
```

and three optional capabilities the view probes by type assertion — the router's
own idiom for `FooterView` and `FramelessView`:

| Interface | Method | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Timestamped` | `SetTimestamps(bool)` | `t` |
| `Followable` | `FollowCmd() *exec.Cmd` | `ctrl+f` |
| `Pageable` | `PagerCmd() *exec.Cmd` | `e` |

`ctrl+r` (reload) needs no interface — every source loads.

CLAUDE.md's warning about `HeaderView` applies: an interface probed silently is
a good behaviour with a bad failure mode. Here each is a **single method**, so
there is no half-satisfied case to fall into — which is precisely why they are
three interfaces rather than one with three methods.

Implementations: `FileSource` (workspaces), `DockerInspectSource` and
`DockerLogsSource` (containers). Only the last one implements all three
optional interfaces.

### The log format is declared, never sniffed

`KindLog` comes from the producer or from a `.log` extension. There is no content
sniff for it — "this looks like a log" is not a decidable question, and the
registry `provider` field is the precedent: *declared, never sniffed from the
URL*, so registration order decides nothing.

JSON and XML keep their content sniff, but only as a **fallback for a file with
no useful extension**. The extension wins when there is one.

### A line with no level is never hidden by accident

This is the decision the whole filter rests on. A stack trace is a dozen lines
with no level on them; a filter set to *≥ warn* that drops them has destroyed
exactly what the user opened the logs to read.

So an unlevelled line **inherits the level of the line above it**, and a line
before any levelled line is `LevelUnknown`, which every filter shows. The
trade-off, stated so it is not discovered later: a genuinely unrelated
unlevelled line following an `INFO` is filtered out with it. That is the
behaviour `lnav` and `stern` settled on, and it is the right side of the trade —
losing a stray line beats losing a stack trace.

Levels are recognised in three shapes, in this order, because a Docker log is
just as likely to be any of them:

1. **JSON lines** — `{"level":"error",…}`, `"severity"`, `"lvl"`
2. **logfmt** — `level=error`, `lvl=warn`
3. **bare text** — a token in the first ~48 characters: `FATAL` `PANIC` `ERROR`
   `ERRO` `ERR` `WARN` `WARNING` `WRN` `INFO` `INF` `DEBUG` `DBG` `TRACE`

### Verbosity is one cycling minimum, not four toggles

`v` cycles `all → debug → info → warn → error`, shown as one `FilterBar` token
(`≥ warn`). One key rather than four, it is what "niveau de verbosité" means, and
it is **monotone** — which log levels are. Nobody wants *warn but not error*.

`components.FilterBar` is used, not a local filter (Rule 136), with
`NewFilterBarWithTokens` exactly as the netdiag ports tab does. That also brings
`/` text search to the text pane for free — which closes the gap the first draft
of this plan left open on a 400-line `docker inspect`.

**If you would rather have four independent toggles** (`e` `w` `i` `d`), say so:
`FilterBar` supports several tokens and the change is confined to one handler.
The monotone cycle is the recommendation.

---

## Patterns to mirror

| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Shared destination view | `internal/app/scan_details.go:90` `openSecurityView` | install a built view, record `OriginView`, `tea.Batch(Init, requestResize)` |
| Return to origin | `internal/app/app.go:349` `security.BackToOriginMsg` | view emits, router calls `switchView(msg.Origin)` |
| Text pane | `internal/ui/containers/update.go:423` `refreshLogsViewport`, `:433` `wrapLines`, `:411` `ansi.Strip` | **moved wholesale**, comments included |
| Filter tokens | `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go` `NewFilterBarWithTokens` | tokens in the footer bar, `/` for text (Rule 136) |
| Optional interface probed | `internal/app/view.go:94` `FramelessView` | type assertion with a safe default |
| Producer does its own I/O | `internal/ui/containers/commands.go:88` `fetchContainerLogs` | `Cmd` fetches, returns a message (Rule 110) |
| Row type carrying decoration | `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/row.go` `explorerRow` | columns built once in `New`, closing over nothing |
| Table of rows | `internal/ui/datatable` | the only way to draw rows; `Cell` plain, colour via `Style` (Rule 122) |
| Footer messages | Rule 128, `internal/ui/workspaces/commands.go:22` | set + 3s timer; never `return m, nil` after setting one |
| Semantic colour aliases | `internal/ui/theme/colors.go:61` severity block | aliases of existing colours; no hex outside the palette (Rule 119) |

No precedent exists for a **tree** or for **syntax highlighting**; both are new
and are stated as such rather than dressed as conventions.

---

## Phase 0 — `internal/viewer`, the domain package (no TUI)

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `document.go` | `Kind` (`KindAuto`, `KindPlain`, `KindJSON`, `KindXML`, `KindLog`), `Document{Name, Kind, Raw, Lines, Root, ParseErr}`, `Open(name string, kind Kind, data []byte) Document` |
| `source.go` | `Source`, `Timestamped`, `Followable`, `Pageable`, `FileSource` |
| `detect.go` | `DetectKind(name, data)` — extension, then a content sniff for JSON/XML only; `IsBinary(data)` |
| `read.go` | the 5 MiB cap and the binary refusal, in one place so every producer gets the same answer |
| `normalize.go` | `ansi.Strip`, `\r\n` → `\n`, stray `\r` dropped — **moved from containers**, unconditional for every document |
| `wrap.go` | `WrapLines(content, width)` — **moved from containers** |
| `json.go` | `parseJSON` via `json.Decoder.Token()` — **ordered**, which `map[string]any` is not |
| `xml.go` | `parseXML` via `xml.Decoder.Token()` — elements, attributes, text, comments |
| `node.go` | `Node{ID int, Key, Value string, Kind NodeKind, Children []*Node}` |
| `log.go` | `LogLine{Level, Text}`, `ParseLog(text) []LogLine`, `Level` and its ordering |
| `highlight.go` | `Tokenize(kind, text) []Token{Class TokenClass, Text string}` — chroma, lexer only |

Decisions worth keeping:

- **A node's identity is an `ID` assigned in parse order**, not a JSONPath. The
  tree is parsed once per open, so an int is stable and the expansion map is
  `map[int]bool` in the view. A path string is a second representation of the
  same thing with more ways to disagree.
- **An XML attribute is a node of its own**, a child of its element — the only
  representation that answers for a document whose information is in its
  attributes, which is most of them.
- **A malformed document is not an error, it is a text document.** `Open`
  records `ParseErr`, falls back to `KindPlain`, and the view says so in the
  footer (`Malformed JSON — showing text`). Refusing to open it would hide
  precisely the content needed to fix it.
- **`ReadFile` refuses two things and names both**: over `MaxSize` (5 MiB) and
  binary (a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB). A refusal is a footer error, never a
  screen. The cap is a *file* concern — a source that fetches (`docker logs
  --tail 500`) is bounded by its own command.
- The invariant everything rests on — **concatenating every token's text
  reproduces the input exactly** — gets a test of its own.

## Phase 1 — theme colours

`internal/ui/theme/colors.go` gains a syntax block of **semantic aliases**, in
the section that references the palette rather than declaring hex (Rule 119):

```go
ColorSyntaxKey     = ColorSecondary
ColorSyntaxString  = ColorOK
ColorSyntaxNumber  = ColorHighlight
ColorSyntaxLiteral = ColorPrimary   // true / false / null
ColorSyntaxPunct   = ColorDim
ColorSyntaxTag     = ColorSecondary
ColorSyntaxAttr    = ColorPrimary
ColorSyntaxComment = ColorDim
```

No theme file changes: the six files in `themes/` declare no syntax keys, so
every theme gets a coherent palette for free and a future theme can override
them by adding keys — the escape hatch the severity colours already have.

**Log levels get no new colours.** `StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`,
`DimStyle` and the default text colour already mean exactly error / warn / debug
/ info. Adding `ColorLogError = ColorError` would be a third name for one thing.

The `TokenClass → lipgloss.Style` mapping lives in
`internal/ui/viewer/syntax.go`, which imports both `internal/viewer` and
`theme`, so nothing new is coupled.

## Phase 2 — `internal/ui/viewer`, the view

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `model.go` | `Model`, `New(cfg)`, `NewWithSource(cfg, src)` |
| `messages.go` | `OpenRequestMsg{Source}`, `LoadedMsg`, `BackToOriginMsg{Origin}` |
| `tree.go` | `treeRow`, two columns, `rebuildRows()` |
| `text.go` | the text pane: highlight once, wrap on demand, level filter |
| `syntax.go` | `TokenClass` → style |
| `update.go` | keys, resize, the source capability probes |
| `view.go` | `View`, `HeaderView` (all four), `FooterView`, `help.Provider`, `InEditMode` |

### The tree is a `datatable`, the text pane is a `viewport`

CLAUDE.md: *every table in the application is a `datatable`; there is no second
way to build one*. The tree qualifies — two columns, **Key** and **Value**, with
the indentation and the expand chevron as plain text inside the Key cell
(Rule 122). It buys the width solver (Rule 116), the cursor clamp and the
selected-row rendering.

It works here for a reason worth stating: **a tree cell holds exactly one syntax
class**, so one `Style` per cell is enough. `datatable` cannot express several
colours inside one cell and never has to.

Neither column sets `Less` or `Search`. Sorting a JSON tree destroys the order
the file gave it — which is why `json.Decoder.Token()` is used at all — and a
text filter hides parents and orphans their children. `.` and `/` are therefore
unbound in the tree, and the shortcut list says so by omission (Rule 138).

The text pane is a `viewport.Model`, the containers logs pane moved. Rule 122
does not apply — it is not a table — so a line may carry many colours. **Rule 115
does**: every token style sets `Background(theme.ColorBackground)` and every line
is padded with `theme.PadWithBg`, or one reset mid-line shows the terminal's own
background for the rest of it.

### Highlighting and filtering are computed once

Tokenising 5 MiB per frame is not viable, and neither is re-filtering 500 log
lines. The rendered lines are rebuilt when the document loads, when `c`, `w` or
`v` changes, and when the width changes with wrap on — nowhere else. `View()`
stays read-only (Rule 110).

### Keys

| Key | Effect | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| `↑↓` `g` `G` `pgup/pgdn` | move / scroll | always (omitted from `GetShortcuts`, Rule 138) |
| `←` / `→` | collapse / expand | tree display |
| `f` | switch display: tree ↔ text | structured document |
| `c` | syntax highlighting on / off | always |
| `w` | soft wrap | text display |
| `v` | verbosity: `all · debug · info · warn · error` | `KindLog` |
| `/` | search the text | text display |
| `t` | timestamps | source is `Timestamped` |
| `ctrl+r` | reload | always |
| `ctrl+f` | follow live output | source is `Followable` |
| `e` | open in the system pager | source is `Pageable` |
| `esc` | back to the origin view | always |

Three collisions were resolved rather than accepted:

- **`h`/`l` stay unbound.** Rule 111 reserves them as `←`/`→` aliases, which is
  exactly the tree's collapse and expand. That is why the highlight toggle is
  `c` (coloration), not `h`.
- **Follow moved from `f` to `ctrl+f`.** `f` is the display toggle; `F` would
  read as a variant of it. `ctrl+r` and `ctrl+f` now sit together as *reload
  once* and *reload continuously*, which is what they are.
- **`q` no longer closes.** The logs pane accepted `esc` or `q`; `q` is the
  application-level quit key (Rule 111) and a view that swallows it is the
  exception, not the rule. `esc` alone.

### Header

`GetTitle()` → `󱀫 Viewer · <name>`. `GetHeaderInfo` carries `Context`, `Format`
(`json · tree`, `json · text`, `log · ≥ warn`) and `Lines` or `Nodes`. All four
`HeaderView` methods are implemented — CLAUDE.md notes that supplying two of them
satisfies nothing and renders an empty title in silence.

An empty viewer renders `Nothing open` and advertises `esc`. It exists so
`createView` can build one for the router's contract test.

## Phase 3 — router wiring

- `command.ViewViewer ViewType = "viewer"`, **deliberately absent from
  `viewNames`**: `:viewer` on an empty viewer is a screen saying nothing, and the
  configuration view's `default_view` would offer it as a landing view — the
  defect `ViewNames()` was split from `FullNames()` to fix.
- `internal/command/parser.go` gains `AllViewNames()` = `ViewNames()` plus the
  router-only views. `TestEveryViewSuppliesItsHeaderAndHelp` and
  `TestOnlyTheDashboardIsFrameless` iterate it; `default_view` and completion
  keep `ViewNames()`.
- `createView`: `case command.ViewViewer: a.views[view] = viewer.New(a.config)`.
- `internal/app/viewer.go`: `handleViewerOpenRequest` sets
  `OriginView = a.currentView`, installs, switches, `tea.Batch(Init,
  requestResize)`; `case viewer.BackToOriginMsg: return a, a.switchView(msg.Origin)`.

The router does **no I/O**: the message carries a `Source` and the view loads it
in its own `Init`. That is the difference from `handleWorkspaceScanDetails`,
which loads a cache file the router owns.

## Phase 4 — workspaces opens a file

`enter` already means *scan details*, and only for a git repository with a cached
result. A file is never a git repository, so the branches cannot collide:
`openScanDetails` gains an early branch returning
`viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: viewer.NewFileSource(entry.Path)}` for `!entry.IsDir`.

The read happens in the viewer's `Init`, so a refusal (too large, binary) is a
footer error *in the viewer* rather than in workspaces — one place that decides,
one place that reports.

`GetShortcuts` gains `{enter, "View file"}` when the selection is a file
(Rule 130); `GetHelpContent` gains a **Viewing files** section in the same commit
(Rule 114). `ModeSelecting` is untouched — `enter` there confirms a directory.

## Phase 5 — containers: `i` and `l` both open the viewer

- `internal/docker/client.go` gains `Inspect(id) ([]byte, error)`, keeping the
  existing `docker.IsContainerID` guard. `GetContainerLogs` already exists.
- `i` → `viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: DockerInspectSource{ID, Name}}`.
- `l` → `viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: DockerLogsSource{ID, Name, Tail: 500}}`.
- Both sources live in `internal/ui/containers/sources.go`: they know docker,
  and `internal/viewer` must not.
- **Every pager path goes**, and the Windows branches with them — the temp files
  (`%TEMP%\devdesk-inspect.txt`, `devdesk-logs.txt`) and the `more` fallback
  existed only because `less` is absent on Windows. The viewer is the answer on
  every platform. The `e` escape hatch survives only for logs, through
  `Pageable`, because `less` still handles a gigabyte better than a `viewport`
  does.
- The deletion list at the top of this plan applies here.
- `GetShortcuts` keeps `{i, "Inspect"}` and `{l, "Logs"}`; the help entries stop
  naming `less`, `q`, `w`, `t` and `f`, which now belong to the viewer (Rule 114).

## Phase 6 — one configuration setting *(confirm)*

`config.AppConfig` gains `SyntaxHighlight bool` (`yaml:"syntax_highlight"`,
default true), with one row in the configuration view's `app` tab
(`internal/ui/configuration/fields.go`).

It is the default the viewer **opens** with, and the viewer never writes it: `c`
changes session state only. The configuration view stays the single writer —
which is the whole point of `applyThemeNow` replacing the old theme picker.

Say the word and this phase drops; the viewer then opens with highlighting on.

## Phase 7 — tests, docs, backlog

---

## Files to change

| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/viewer/*.go` | CREATE | domain package, 11 files, ~850 lines (two moved from containers) |
| `internal/ui/viewer/*.go` | CREATE | the view, 7 files, ~800 lines |
| `internal/app/viewer.go` | CREATE | router handler + return-to-origin |
| `internal/ui/containers/sources.go` | CREATE | the two docker sources |
| `internal/app/app.go` | UPDATE | two cases in `Update` |
| `internal/app/command_line.go` | UPDATE | `createView` case |
| `internal/command/parser.go` | UPDATE | `ViewViewer`, `AllViewNames()` |
| `internal/app/view_contract_test.go` | UPDATE | iterate `AllViewNames()` |
| `internal/ui/theme/colors.go` | UPDATE | the syntax alias block |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/{update,actions,view}.go` | UPDATE | `enter` on a file, shortcuts, help |
| `internal/ui/containers/{model,update,view,commands}.go` | UPDATE | **the logs pane is removed**; `i` and `l` emit open requests |
| `internal/docker/client.go` | UPDATE | `Inspect` |
| `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go` | UPDATE | `syntax_highlight` (phase 6) |
| `go.mod` / `go.sum` | UPDATE | chroma v2 |
| `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | UPDATE | a Viewer section; the containers logs and inspect lines |
| `docs/backlog.md` | UPDATE | §3.25 |

`internal/ui/containers/update.go` is 707 lines today and drops well under 500 —
progress against §2's 800-line ceiling. No new file exceeds 250.

## Tests

**`internal/viewer`**
- `TestAJSONObjectKeepsTheOrderTheFileGaveIt`
- `TestXMLAttributesAreNodesOfTheirOwn`
- `TestAMalformedJSONOpensAsTextAndSaysSo`
- `TestABinaryFileIsRefusedRatherThanRendered`
- `TestAFileOverTheSizeCapIsRefused`
- `TestDetectionPrefersTheExtensionThenTheContent`
- `TestALogKindIsNeverInferredFromContent`
- `TestAnUnlevelledLineInheritsTheLineAbove` — the stack-trace case
- `TestLevelsAreReadFromJSONLogfmtAndBareText`
- `TestNormalizationStripsANSIAndCarriageReturns`
- `TestHighlightingReproducesTheInputExactly` — the chroma invariant

**`internal/ui/viewer`**
- `TestCollapsingANodeHidesItsDescendants`
- `TestTheCursorStaysOnARowThatSurvivesACollapse`
- `TestAPlainDocumentOffersNoDisplayToggle` (Rule 130)
- `TestOnlyALogDocumentOffersTheVerbosityFilter`
- `TestVerbosityIsMonotone` — `≥ warn` shows errors
- `TestTimestampsAndFollowAppearOnlyForASourceThatSupportsThem`
- `TestEveryTreeCellIsPlainText` (Rule 122)
- `TestEveryTextLineCarriesTheAppBackground` (Rule 115)
- `TestTheHeaderNamesTheFormatAndTheFilter`

**`internal/app`**
- `TestAViewerOpenRequestRecordsWhereItCameFrom`
- `TestEscFromTheViewerReturnsToItsOrigin`
- `TestTheViewerIsNotTypeableAsACommand`
- the two contract tests, now over `AllViewNames()`

**`internal/ui/workspaces`**
- `TestEnterOnAFileAsksForTheViewer`
- `TestEnterOnAScannedGitRepoStillOpensScanDetails`
- `TestTheViewFileShortcutAppearsOnlyForAFile`

**`internal/ui/containers`**

# Plan: A viewer for documents — text, JSON, XML and logs

**Source**: free-form request (2026-08-16), revised after the logs-reuse note
**Backlog entry to write**: `docs/backlog.md` §3.25
**Complexity**: Large (new domain package + new view + three producers + one dependency),
but **net-negative in `internal/ui/containers`**, which loses its whole logs pane.

## Summary

A new view — `viewer` — displays a document read-only. A JSON or an XML document
opens on a **navigable tree**; either can be switched to its **own text**, with
syntax highlighting on or off. A **log** document opens as text with a verbosity
filter.

Three producers, one destination:

| Producer | Key | Document |
|---|---|---|
| `workspaces` | `enter` on a file | detected from the extension, then the content |
| `containers` | `i` | `docker inspect` — JSON |
| `containers` | `l` | `docker logs` — log |

That is the shape the security view already has (opened from workspaces *and*
from the OCI images list), and it is built the same way: the producer hands the
router one message, the router installs the view and records where `esc` returns.

## What this deletes

The containers view already owns a text pane — `stateLogs`, a `viewport`, soft
wrap, ANSI stripping, CR normalisation, scroll keys, reload, an external pager,
follow and a timestamps toggle. **None of it is containers-specific except the
last three**, and those are properties of *where the text came from*, not of the
pane. So the pane moves into the viewer and containers loses:

`viewState` · `stateLogs` · `logsViewport` · `logsContainerID` ·
`logsContainerName` · `logsLoading` · `logsRawContent` · `logsWrapEnabled` ·
`logsTimestamps` · `handleLogsKeyMsg` · `refreshLogsViewport` · `wrapLines` ·
`toggleLogsWrap` · `toggleLogsTimestamps` · `openExternalPager` ·
`followContainerLogs` · `handleContainerLogsLoaded` · `ContainerLogsLoadedMsg` ·
`inspectSelectedContainer`'s pager path · the `stateLogs` branches in
`InEditMode`, `GetFooterHeight`, `RenderFooter`, `GetShortcuts`, `View` and
`resize`.

`wrapLines` and the ANSI/CR normalisation are **moved**, not rewritten — they are
correct, and the reasons in their comments (systemd colours the output, progress
bars overwrite with `\r`) apply to any text this app displays, not just to logs.

`PagerExitMsg` stays: the shell path still uses it. Only its `stateLogs` branch
goes.

---

## Decisions taken

### Two display axes, not four names — **confirmed**

The request named *tree*, *raw*, *plain text* and a highlight toggle. Four names,
two independent facts:

| Axis | Values | Key |
|---|---|---|
| Display | `tree` or `text` | `f` |
| Highlight | on / off | `c` |

"Plain text" is `text` with colour off. A third display that additionally
discarded the detected format was put to the user and declined: it would make
`plain + colour on` and `text + colour off` two names for one screen. A document
with no structure (`.md`, `.go`, a log) is always `text`, and `f` is hidden for it
(Rule 130).

### chroma as a lexer, never as a formatter — **confirmed**

`github.com/alecthomas/chroma/v2` (v2.27.0, pure Go, no cgo), chosen over ~250
hand-written lines of escape and CDATA handling, and the only route to Go, YAML
or Dockerfile later. It embeds every lexer, so the binary grows by a few MB —
the accepted cost, to be measured and recorded in §3.25.

`chroma/v2/formatters` is **never imported**. It writes its own ANSI colour and
reset sequences, and a reset inside a line strips the app background for
everything after it (Rule 115). Only `lexers.Get(...).Tokenise` is used; the
classes are mapped to theme styles by the UI package.

### A source, not a byte slice

The logs pane can reload, follow and re-fetch with timestamps. A viewer holding
only `[]byte` cannot do any of that, and neither could it reload a file the user
has just edited. So a document carries **where it came from**:

```go
type Source interface {
    Name() string                 // what the header shows
    Kind() Kind                   // declared by the producer, or KindAuto
    Load() ([]byte, error)
}
```

and three optional capabilities the view probes by type assertion — the router's
own idiom for `FooterView` and `FramelessView`:

| Interface | Method | Unlocks |
|---|---|---|
| `Timestamped` | `SetTimestamps(bool)` | `t` |
| `Followable` | `FollowCmd() *exec.Cmd` | `ctrl+f` |
| `Pageable` | `PagerCmd() *exec.Cmd` | `e` |

`ctrl+r` (reload) needs no interface — every source loads.

CLAUDE.md's warning about `HeaderView` applies: an interface probed silently is
a good behaviour with a bad failure mode. Here each is a **single method**, so
there is no half-satisfied case to fall into — which is precisely why they are
three interfaces rather than one with three methods.

Implementations: `FileSource` (workspaces), `DockerInspectSource` and
`DockerLogsSource` (containers). Only the last one implements all three
optional interfaces.

### The log format is declared, never sniffed

`KindLog` comes from the producer or from a `.log` extension. There is no content
sniff for it — "this looks like a log" is not a decidable question, and the
registry `provider` field is the precedent: *declared, never sniffed from the
URL*, so registration order decides nothing.

JSON and XML keep their content sniff, but only as a **fallback for a file with
no useful extension**. The extension wins when there is one.

### A line with no level is never hidden by accident

This is the decision the whole filter rests on. A stack trace is a dozen lines
with no level on them; a filter set to *≥ warn* that drops them has destroyed
exactly what the user opened the logs to read.

So an unlevelled line **inherits the level of the line above it**, and a line
before any levelled line is `LevelUnknown`, which every filter shows. The
trade-off, stated so it is not discovered later: a genuinely unrelated
unlevelled line following an `INFO` is filtered out with it. That is the
behaviour `lnav` and `stern` settled on, and it is the right side of the trade —
losing a stray line beats losing a stack trace.

Levels are recognised in three shapes, in this order, because a Docker log is
just as likely to be any of them:

1. **JSON lines** — `{"level":"error",…}`, `"severity"`, `"lvl"`
2. **logfmt** — `level=error`, `lvl=warn`
3. **bare text** — a token in the first ~48 characters: `FATAL` `PANIC` `ERROR`
   `ERRO` `ERR` `WARN` `WARNING` `WRN` `INFO` `INF` `DEBUG` `DBG` `TRACE`

### Verbosity is one cycling minimum, not four toggles

`v` cycles `all → debug → info → warn → error`, shown as one `FilterBar` token
(`≥ warn`). One key rather than four, it is what "niveau de verbosité" means, and
it is **monotone** — which log levels are. Nobody wants *warn but not error*.

`components.FilterBar` is used, not a local filter (Rule 136), with
`NewFilterBarWithTokens` exactly as the netdiag ports tab does. That also brings
`/` text search to the text pane for free — which closes the gap the first draft
of this plan left open on a 400-line `docker inspect`.

**If you would rather have four independent toggles** (`e` `w` `i` `d`), say so:
`FilterBar` supports several tokens and the change is confined to one handler.
The monotone cycle is the recommendation.

---

## Patterns to mirror

| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Shared destination view | `internal/app/scan_details.go:90` `openSecurityView` | install a built view, record `OriginView`, `tea.Batch(Init, requestResize)` |
| Return to origin | `internal/app/app.go:349` `security.BackToOriginMsg` | view emits, router calls `switchView(msg.Origin)` |
| Text pane | `internal/ui/containers/update.go:423` `refreshLogsViewport`, `:433` `wrapLines`, `:411` `ansi.Strip` | **moved wholesale**, comments included |
| Filter tokens | `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go` `NewFilterBarWithTokens` | tokens in the footer bar, `/` for text (Rule 136) |
| Optional interface probed | `internal/app/view.go:94` `FramelessView` | type assertion with a safe default |
| Producer does its own I/O | `internal/ui/containers/commands.go:88` `fetchContainerLogs` | `Cmd` fetches, returns a message (Rule 110) |
| Row type carrying decoration | `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/row.go` `explorerRow` | columns built once in `New`, closing over nothing |
| Table of rows | `internal/ui/datatable` | the only way to draw rows; `Cell` plain, colour via `Style` (Rule 122) |
| Footer messages | Rule 128, `internal/ui/workspaces/commands.go:22` | set + 3s timer; never `return m, nil` after setting one |
| Semantic colour aliases | `internal/ui/theme/colors.go:61` severity block | aliases of existing colours; no hex outside the palette (Rule 119) |

No precedent exists for a **tree** or for **syntax highlighting**; both are new
and are stated as such rather than dressed as conventions.

---

## Phase 0 — `internal/viewer`, the domain package (no TUI)

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `document.go` | `Kind` (`KindAuto`, `KindPlain`, `KindJSON`, `KindXML`, `KindLog`), `Document{Name, Kind, Raw, Lines, Root, ParseErr}`, `Open(name string, kind Kind, data []byte) Document` |
| `source.go` | `Source`, `Timestamped`, `Followable`, `Pageable`, `FileSource` |
| `detect.go` | `DetectKind(name, data)` — extension, then a content sniff for JSON/XML only; `IsBinary(data)` |
| `read.go` | the 5 MiB cap and the binary refusal, in one place so every producer gets the same answer |
| `normalize.go` | `ansi.Strip`, `\r\n` → `\n`, stray `\r` dropped — **moved from containers**, unconditional for every document |
| `wrap.go` | `WrapLines(content, width)` — **moved from containers** |
| `json.go` | `parseJSON` via `json.Decoder.Token()` — **ordered**, which `map[string]any` is not |
| `xml.go` | `parseXML` via `xml.Decoder.Token()` — elements, attributes, text, comments |
| `node.go` | `Node{ID int, Key, Value string, Kind NodeKind, Children []*Node}` |
| `log.go` | `LogLine{Level, Text}`, `ParseLog(text) []LogLine`, `Level` and its ordering |
| `highlight.go` | `Tokenize(kind, text) []Token{Class TokenClass, Text string}` — chroma, lexer only |

Decisions worth keeping:

- **A node's identity is an `ID` assigned in parse order**, not a JSONPath. The
  tree is parsed once per open, so an int is stable and the expansion map is
  `map[int]bool` in the view. A path string is a second representation of the
  same thing with more ways to disagree.
- **An XML attribute is a node of its own**, a child of its element — the only
  representation that answers for a document whose information is in its
  attributes, which is most of them.
- **A malformed document is not an error, it is a text document.** `Open`
  records `ParseErr`, falls back to `KindPlain`, and the view says so in the
  footer (`Malformed JSON — showing text`). Refusing to open it would hide
  precisely the content needed to fix it.
- **`ReadFile` refuses two things and names both**: over `MaxSize` (5 MiB) and
  binary (a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB). A refusal is a footer error, never a
  screen. The cap is a *file* concern — a source that fetches (`docker logs
  --tail 500`) is bounded by its own command.
- The invariant everything rests on — **concatenating every token's text
  reproduces the input exactly** — gets a test of its own.

## Phase 1 — theme colours

`internal/ui/theme/colors.go` gains a syntax block of **semantic aliases**, in
the section that references the palette rather than declaring hex (Rule 119):

```go
ColorSyntaxKey     = ColorSecondary
ColorSyntaxString  = ColorOK
ColorSyntaxNumber  = ColorHighlight
ColorSyntaxLiteral = ColorPrimary   // true / false / null
ColorSyntaxPunct   = ColorDim
ColorSyntaxTag     = ColorSecondary
ColorSyntaxAttr    = ColorPrimary
ColorSyntaxComment = ColorDim
```

No theme file changes: the six files in `themes/` declare no syntax keys, so
every theme gets a coherent palette for free and a future theme can override
them by adding keys — the escape hatch the severity colours already have.

**Log levels get no new colours.** `StatusErrorStyle`, `StatusWarningStyle`,
`DimStyle` and the default text colour already mean exactly error / warn / debug
/ info. Adding `ColorLogError = ColorError` would be a third name for one thing.

The `TokenClass → lipgloss.Style` mapping lives in
`internal/ui/viewer/syntax.go`, which imports both `internal/viewer` and
`theme`, so nothing new is coupled.

## Phase 2 — `internal/ui/viewer`, the view

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `model.go` | `Model`, `New(cfg)`, `NewWithSource(cfg, src)` |
| `messages.go` | `OpenRequestMsg{Source}`, `LoadedMsg`, `BackToOriginMsg{Origin}` |
| `tree.go` | `treeRow`, two columns, `rebuildRows()` |
| `text.go` | the text pane: highlight once, wrap on demand, level filter |
| `syntax.go` | `TokenClass` → style |
| `update.go` | keys, resize, the source capability probes |
| `view.go` | `View`, `HeaderView` (all four), `FooterView`, `help.Provider`, `InEditMode` |

### The tree is a `datatable`, the text pane is a `viewport`

CLAUDE.md: *every table in the application is a `datatable`; there is no second
way to build one*. The tree qualifies — two columns, **Key** and **Value**, with
the indentation and the expand chevron as plain text inside the Key cell
(Rule 122). It buys the width solver (Rule 116), the cursor clamp and the
selected-row rendering.

It works here for a reason worth stating: **a tree cell holds exactly one syntax
class**, so one `Style` per cell is enough. `datatable` cannot express several
colours inside one cell and never has to.

Neither column sets `Less` or `Search`. Sorting a JSON tree destroys the order
the file gave it — which is why `json.Decoder.Token()` is used at all — and a
text filter hides parents and orphans their children. `.` and `/` are therefore
unbound in the tree, and the shortcut list says so by omission (Rule 138).

The text pane is a `viewport.Model`, the containers logs pane moved. Rule 122
does not apply — it is not a table — so a line may carry many colours. **Rule 115
does**: every token style sets `Background(theme.ColorBackground)` and every line
is padded with `theme.PadWithBg`, or one reset mid-line shows the terminal's own
background for the rest of it.

### Highlighting and filtering are computed once

Tokenising 5 MiB per frame is not viable, and neither is re-filtering 500 log
lines. The rendered lines are rebuilt when the document loads, when `c`, `w` or
`v` changes, and when the width changes with wrap on — nowhere else. `View()`
stays read-only (Rule 110).

### Keys

| Key | Effect | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| `↑↓` `g` `G` `pgup/pgdn` | move / scroll | always (omitted from `GetShortcuts`, Rule 138) |
| `←` / `→` | collapse / expand | tree display |
| `f` | switch display: tree ↔ text | structured document |
| `c` | syntax highlighting on / off | always |
| `w` | soft wrap | text display |
| `v` | verbosity: `all · debug · info · warn · error` | `KindLog` |
| `/` | search the text | text display |
| `t` | timestamps | source is `Timestamped` |
| `ctrl+r` | reload | always |
| `ctrl+f` | follow live output | source is `Followable` |
| `e` | open in the system pager | source is `Pageable` |
| `esc` | back to the origin view | always |

Three collisions were resolved rather than accepted:

- **`h`/`l` stay unbound.** Rule 111 reserves them as `←`/`→` aliases, which is
  exactly the tree's collapse and expand. That is why the highlight toggle is
  `c` (coloration), not `h`.
- **Follow moved from `f` to `ctrl+f`.** `f` is the display toggle; `F` would
  read as a variant of it. `ctrl+r` and `ctrl+f` now sit together as *reload
  once* and *reload continuously*, which is what they are.
- **`q` no longer closes.** The logs pane accepted `esc` or `q`; `q` is the
  application-level quit key (Rule 111) and a view that swallows it is the
  exception, not the rule. `esc` alone.

### Header

`GetTitle()` → `󱀫 Viewer · <name>`. `GetHeaderInfo` carries `Context`, `Format`
(`json · tree`, `json · text`, `log · ≥ warn`) and `Lines` or `Nodes`. All four
`HeaderView` methods are implemented — CLAUDE.md notes that supplying two of them
satisfies nothing and renders an empty title in silence.

An empty viewer renders `Nothing open` and advertises `esc`. It exists so
`createView` can build one for the router's contract test.

## Phase 3 — router wiring

- `command.ViewViewer ViewType = "viewer"`, **deliberately absent from
  `viewNames`**: `:viewer` on an empty viewer is a screen saying nothing, and the
  configuration view's `default_view` would offer it as a landing view — the
  defect `ViewNames()` was split from `FullNames()` to fix.
- `internal/command/parser.go` gains `AllViewNames()` = `ViewNames()` plus the
  router-only views. `TestEveryViewSuppliesItsHeaderAndHelp` and
  `TestOnlyTheDashboardIsFrameless` iterate it; `default_view` and completion
  keep `ViewNames()`.
- `createView`: `case command.ViewViewer: a.views[view] = viewer.New(a.config)`.
- `internal/app/viewer.go`: `handleViewerOpenRequest` sets
  `OriginView = a.currentView`, installs, switches, `tea.Batch(Init,
  requestResize)`; `case viewer.BackToOriginMsg: return a, a.switchView(msg.Origin)`.

The router does **no I/O**: the message carries a `Source` and the view loads it
in its own `Init`. That is the difference from `handleWorkspaceScanDetails`,
which loads a cache file the router owns.

## Phase 4 — workspaces opens a file

`enter` already means *scan details*, and only for a git repository with a cached
result. A file is never a git repository, so the branches cannot collide:
`openScanDetails` gains an early branch returning
`viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: viewer.NewFileSource(entry.Path)}` for `!entry.IsDir`.

The read happens in the viewer's `Init`, so a refusal (too large, binary) is a
footer error *in the viewer* rather than in workspaces — one place that decides,
one place that reports.

`GetShortcuts` gains `{enter, "View file"}` when the selection is a file
(Rule 130); `GetHelpContent` gains a **Viewing files** section in the same commit
(Rule 114). `ModeSelecting` is untouched — `enter` there confirms a directory.

## Phase 5 — containers: `i` and `l` both open the viewer

- `internal/docker/client.go` gains `Inspect(id) ([]byte, error)`, keeping the

- `i` → `viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: DockerInspectSource{ID, Name}}`.
- `l` → `viewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: DockerLogsSource{ID, Name, Tail: 500}}`.
- Both sources live in `internal/ui/containers/sources.go`: they know docker,

- **Every pager path goes**, and the Windows branches with them — the temp files

  every platform. The `e` escape hatch survives only for logs, through
  `Pageable`, because `less` still handles a gigabyte better than a `viewport`

- The deletion list at the top of this plan applies here.
- `GetShortcuts` keeps `{i, "Inspect"}` and `{l, "Logs"}`; the help entries stop

## Phase 6 — one configuration setting *(confirm)*

`config.AppConfig` gains `SyntaxHighlight bool` (`yaml:"syntax_highlight"`,
default true), with one row in the configuration view's `app` tab
(`internal/ui/configuration/fields.go`).

It is the default the viewer **opens** with, and the viewer never writes it: `c`
changes session state only. The configuration view stays the single writer —
which is the whole point of `applyThemeNow` replacing the old theme picker.

Say the word and this phase drops; the viewer then opens with highlighting on.

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| chroma embeds every lexer (several MB) | HIGH — certain | Decided. Measure the delta and record it in §3.25 so the cost is on the record rather than assumed |
| Moving the logs pane regresses behaviour nobody re-tested | MEDIUM | The existing logs tests move with the code instead of being deleted; that is what makes this a move rather than a rewrite |
| An unlevelled line is filtered away with its parent | MEDIUM | Inheritance is the stated trade; `all` is the default verbosity, so nothing is hidden until the user asks |
| Highlighting or filtering on every frame | MEDIUM | Rebuilt on load / `c` / `w` / `v` / width only; `View()` read-only |
| An ANSI reset inside a line strips the app background (Rule 115) | MEDIUM | chroma formatters never used; every token style sets the background; a test asserts it |
| A source capability interface silently unsatisfied | LOW | Each is a single method — there is no half-satisfied case, unlike `HeaderView` |
| `AllViewNames()` drifts from the `createView` switch | LOW | The contract test iterates it and fails on a missing case |
| A minified JSON is one enormous line in the text display | LOW | `w` wraps; the tree is the answer and is the default |

content.text:
Plan revised. You were right — the containers logs pane is most of the text pane already, and folding it in makes containers **smaller**.

## What changed

**`internal/ui/containers` loses its whole logs pane.** `viewState`, `logsViewport`, `logsRawContent`, `logsWrapEnabled`, `logsTimestamps`, `handleLogsKeyMsg`, `refreshLogsViewport`, `wrapLines`, `toggleLogsWrap`, `toggleLogsTimestamps`, `openExternalPager`, `followContainerLogs`, `handleContainerLogsLoaded`, plus the `stateLogs` branches in six methods. `update.go` goes from 707 lines to under 500 — progress against §2's ceiling.

`wrapLines` and the ANSI/CR normalisation are **moved, comments included** — the reasons in them (systemd colours the output, progress bars overwrite with `\r`) apply to any text this app shows, not just logs. And the existing logs scroll/resize tests move to the viewer rather than being deleted, which is what makes this a move and not a rewrite.

**A document carries a `Source`, not a byte slice.** Reload, follow and timestamps are properties of *where the text came from*. Three single-method optional interfaces the view probes — `Timestamped`, `Followable`, `Pageable` — so `t`, `ctrl+f` and `e` appear only for the logs source (Rule 130). Single-method on purpose: there's no half-satisfied case to fall into, which is the `HeaderView` trap CLAUDE.md warns about.

**Three key collisions resolved**, not accepted: follow moves `f` → `ctrl+f` (`f` is the display toggle; `ctrl+r`/`ctrl+f` now read as *reload once* / *reload continuously*), `h`/`l` stay unbound because Rule 111 owns them as `←`/`→`, and `q` stops closing the pane — it's the app quit key.

**The filter uses `components.FilterBar`** with tokens, exactly as netdiag's ports tab does (Rule 136). That also brings `/` search to the text pane, which closes the gap the first draft left on a 400-line `docker inspect`.

## The decision I'd most want you to check

A line with **no level inherits the level of the line above it**. A stack trace is a dozen unlevelled lines; a `≥ warn` filter that drops them destroys exactly what you opened the logs to read. The cost: a genuinely unrelated unlevelled line after an `INFO` gets filtered out with it. That's the `lnav`/`stern` trade and I think it's the right side of it.

Plan is settled — `.claude/plans/document-viewer.md`, six phases, no open questions.

**Decided:** two display axes (`f` tree↔text, `c` colour) · chroma as a lexer only, formatters never imported · a `Source` with three single-method capability interfaces · log kind declared, never sniffed · an unlevelled line inherits the one above it · `v` cycles a monotone minimum level · no config setting.

**Net effect on the codebase:** one new domain package, one new view, and `internal/ui/containers` gets *smaller* — its logs pane moves out wholesale, tests included.

Ready to start. Two notes on sequencing before I do:

- I'd go **Phase 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 4**. Phase 5 (containers) is the harder producer and the one that deletes code, so wiring it before workspaces exercises the `Source` interface against the only source that implements all three optional capabilities. Workspaces is then trivial.
- If you'd rather see something running sooner, the smallest end-to-end slice is Phases 0+2+3+5-logs-only: the logs pane moved into the viewer with the verbosity filter, before any JSON tree exists. That proves the move and the filter, and the tree lands on top.

Say **go** for the full sequence, or **logs first** for the thin slice.

1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
30		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
31		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
32		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
33	
34		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
35		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
36	)
37	
38	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
39	type Column[T any] struct {
40		Title string
41		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
42		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
43		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
44		MinWidth int
45		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
46		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
47		Flex int
48		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: it is measured
49		// and truncated before anything is applied to it, and runewidth counts an
50		// escape sequence's bytes as width — a styled string is cut mid-escape and
51		// bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122). Taking a string rather than a
52		// styled value is what makes that unexpressible here.
53		Cell func(T) string
54		// Style colours the cell after it has been measured and truncated, which is
55		// the only order in which colour is safe (see render.go). Nil leaves the
56		// cell in the table's own colours.
57		//
58		// It is not consulted for the selected row: that row is handed to
59		// styles.Selected whole, and a colour inside it would end the highlight
60		// mid-row. A column cannot ask for that back.
61		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
62		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
63		// `.` skips it.
64		Less func(a, b T) bool
65		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
66		// not participate.
67		Search func(T) string
68	}
69	
70	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
71	type Config[T any] struct {
72		Columns []Column[T]
73		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
74		Tokens []components.FilterToken
75		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
76		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
77		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
78		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
79		SortColumn int
80		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
81		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
82		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
83		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
84		SortDesc bool
85		// Key identifies an item across rebuilds, and is what the busy set is held
86		// on. Nil switches the busy facility off entirely, which is the default:
87		// most tables have no action to run on a row.
88		//
89		// It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on this struct instead. Columns are
90		// built once, in New, and close over nothing — imageRow exists because of
91		// that — so a predicate here would have to close over the view's map of
92		// in-flight actions, which is the same trap. Separating the identity from
93		// the state is what avoids it, and it is also what lets IsBusy answer for an
94		// object whose row does not exist yet: the guard on a confirm path runs
95		// before anything is rebuilt.
96		//
97		// Keying on identity rather than a flag on the row is also what survives the
98		// periodic refresh, which replaces the items while an action is running.
99		Key func(T) string
100		// StatusColumn is the column whose cell the spinner replaces while a row is
101		// busy — the one that answers "what about this row". Ignored when Key is
102		// nil.
103		//
104		// That column must not be sortable: askFor reserves width(Title)+2 for a
105		// column carrying a Less, which is expensive for a glyph.
106		StatusColumn int
107		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
108		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
109		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
110		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
111		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
112		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
113	}
114	
115	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
116	type Model[T any] struct {
117		cfg   Config[T]
118		table table.Model
119		bar   components.FilterBar
120	
121		items []T
122		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
123		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
124		// ordering while the screen shows another.
125		visible []T
126	
127		// styles is what was last handed to the table. The rendering is this
128		// package's now (render.go) and bubbles keeps its copy unexported, so the
129		// styles have to be kept on this side to be readable at render time.
130		styles table.Styles
131		// offset is the first visible row — the scroll window bubbles kept in its
132		// viewport. clampOffset owns it.
133		offset int
134	
135		// busy maps an item's Key to the label of the action running on it. Held
136		// here rather than in the view so that one answer — IsBusy — serves the
137		// rendering, the footer and the guard that stops a second command being
138		// issued for the same object.
139		busy map[string]string
140		// spinnerFrame is what a busy row's status cell shows. The frame lives here
141		// and the tick stays in the view: a spinner needs a Cmd, and this package
142		// returns none (Rule 110).
143		spinnerFrame string
144		spinnerIdx   int
145	
146		sortColumn int
147		sortDesc   bool
148		width      int
149	}
150	
151	// New builds a table from its configuration.
152	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
153		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
154		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
155			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
156		}
157		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
158	
159		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
160		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
161			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
162		}
163	
164		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
165		// A frame from the start: a table whose view never calls AdvanceSpinner —
166		// one rendered in the same frame the action began — would otherwise show an
167		// empty status cell, which reads as "nothing is happening".
168		m.AdvanceSpinner()
169		// Through setStyles rather than the table alone: a table rendered before
170		// anything calls applyStyles — one built and drawn in the same frame — would
171		// otherwise render with the zero Styles, which carries no cell padding and
172		// so lays out two cells narrower per column than every width was solved for.
173		m.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
174		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
175		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
176		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
177		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
178		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
179			m.sortColumn = -1
180			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
181			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
182			m.sortDesc = false
183		}
184		return m
185	}
186	
187	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
188	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
189	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
190	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
191	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
192		m.items = items
193		m.rebuild()
194	}
195	
196	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
197	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
198	
199	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
200	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
201	
202	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
203	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
204	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
205		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
206		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
207			var zero T
208			return zero, false
209		}
210		return m.visible[cursor], true
211	}
212	
213	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
214	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
215	
216	// SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
217	// remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
218	// level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
219	func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
220		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
221			return
222		}
223		m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
224		m.afterCursorMove()
225	}
226	
227	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
228	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
229	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
230	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() {
231		m.table.GotoTop()
232		m.afterCursorMove()
233	}
234	
235	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
236	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
237	
238	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
239	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
240	
241	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
242	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
243	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
244		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
245			return true
246		}
247		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
248			if c.Search != nil {
249				return true
250			}
251		}
252		return false
253	}
254	
255	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
256	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
257	
258	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown. The window is re-clamped: a table
259	// that just got shorter can leave the cursor below its own last visible row.
260	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) {
261		m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1))
262		m.clampOffset()
263	}
264	
265	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
266	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
267	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
268		m.table.Focus()
269		m.afterCursorMove()
270	}
271	
272	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
273		m.table.Blur()
274		m.setStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
275	}
276	
277	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
278	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
279	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
280	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
281		m.width = width
282		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
283	
284		cols := m.table.Columns()
285		for i := range cols {
286			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
287			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
288		}
289		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
290		m.bar.Resize(width)
291		if height > 0 {
292			m.SetHeight(height)
293		}
294		m.afterCursorMove() // the selected row is pinned to this width
295	}
296	
297	// The sort arrows, and what they cost. Named because widths.go has to reserve
298	// room for them: a column's MinWidth is the view's statement about its content,
299	// and it knows nothing about two cells this package appends to the header.
300	const (
301		sortArrowAsc  = " ▲"
302		sortArrowDesc = " ▼"
303	)
304	
305	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
306	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
307		if i != m.sortColumn {
308			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
309		}
310		if m.sortDesc {
311			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowDesc
312		}
313		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowAsc
314	}
315	
316	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
317	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
318	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
319	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
320		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
321		if len(sortable) == 0 {
322			return
323		}
324		switch {
325		case m.sortColumn < 0:
326			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
327		case !m.sortDesc:
328			m.sortDesc = true
329		default:
330			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
331		}
332		m.rebuild()
333		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
334	}
335	
336	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
337	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
338	//
339	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
340	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
341	// a branch nothing can ever check.
342	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
343		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
344			return sortable[at+1]
345		}
346		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
347			return -1
348		}
349		return sortable[0]
350	}
351	
352	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
353		var out []int
354		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
355			if c.Less != nil {
356				out = append(out, i)
357			}
358		}
359		return out
360	}
361	
362	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
363	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
364	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
365	
366	// SetSort puts the sort back where the table opened, or anywhere else the view
367	// can name. It exists for the one thing CycleSort cannot express: the registry
368	// browser starts a new search from the default order, and advancing `.` around
369	// the cycle until it comes back is not that.
370	//
371	// A column that cannot be sorted by leaves the table unsorted rather than
372	// silently sorted by something else — the same invariant New settles, so that
373	// nothing downstream has to re-check it.
374	func (m *Model[T]) SetSort(column int, desc bool) {
375		if column < 0 || column >= len(m.cfg.Columns) || m.cfg.Columns[column].Less == nil {
376			column, desc = -1, false
377		}
378		m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = column, desc
379		m.rebuild()
380		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
381	}
382	
383	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
384	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
385	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
386	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
387		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
388			var cmd tea.Cmd
389			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
390			m.rebuild()
391			return cmd
392		}
393	
394		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
395		if !ok {
396			return nil
397		}
398		switch key.String() {
399		case "/":
400			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
401			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
402			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
403			if !m.Searchable() {
404				return nil
405			}
406			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
407		case ".":
408			m.CycleSort()
409		case "up", "k":
410			m.table.MoveUp(1)
411			m.afterCursorMove()
412		case "down", "j":
413			m.table.MoveDown(1)
414			m.afterCursorMove()
415		case "pgup":
416			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
417			m.afterCursorMove()
418		case "pgdown":
419			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
420			m.afterCursorMove()
421		case "g", "home":
422			m.table.GotoTop()
423			m.afterCursorMove()
424		case "G", "end":
425			m.table.GotoBottom()
426			m.afterCursorMove()
427		}
428		return nil
429	}
430	
431	// ── Rows an action is running on ─────────────────────────────────────────────
432	//
433	// A row says two things at once: what the object *is*, and what is *happening*
434	// to it. They have different sources of truth — the state comes back from
435	// docker on the next refresh, the transition is this application's own
436	// knowledge — and different lifetimes. Sharing one glyph is the point; sharing
437	// one function would make every table re-implement the precedence, so the rule
438	// lives here and there is one of it: **busy wins over state**.
439	
440	// MarkBusy records that an action is running on the item with this key, and what
441	// to call it. Call it from Update, never from a Cmd (Rule 110).
442	//
443	// A no-op when the config declares no Key: without one there is nothing to
444	// match a row against, and silently keeping a label nothing can display would
445	// be worse than ignoring it.
446	func (m *Model[T]) MarkBusy(key, label string) {
447		if m.cfg.Key == nil || key == "" {
448			return
449		}
450		if m.busy == nil {
451			m.busy = make(map[string]string, 1)
452		}
453		m.busy[key] = label
454	}
455	
456	// ClearBusy forgets an action.
457	//
458	// It must be called on **every** outcome, the failures included. Clearing only
459	// on success leaves the row spinning for the life of the view, and — worse —
460	// hides the state it still has: a `docker stop` that failed has to read
461	// `running` again, not go on turning.
462	func (m *Model[T]) ClearBusy(key string) { delete(m.busy, key) }
463	
464	// IsBusy reports whether an action is running on this key.
465	//
466	// It answers for an object whose row does not exist yet, which is what makes it
467	// the guard on a confirm path: without it a second keypress on a slow removal
468	// issues a second command, and the second one fails with "no such object" on an
469	// operation that in fact worked.
470	func (m *Model[T]) IsBusy(key string) bool {
471		_, ok := m.busy[key]
472		return ok
473	}
474	
475	// BusyLabels returns what is running, sorted, for a view's footer line. Sorted
476	// because a map's order changes between frames and a footer that reshuffles
477	// itself is unreadable.
478	func (m *Model[T]) BusyLabels() []string {
479		if len(m.busy) == 0 {
480			return nil
481		}
482		out := make([]string, 0, len(m.busy))
483		for _, label := range m.busy {
484			out = append(out, label)
485		}
486		sort.Strings(out)
487		return out
488	}
489	
490	// AdvanceSpinner moves the frame shown on busy rows one step on. Views call it
491	// from the spinner tick they already run.
492	func (m *Model[T]) AdvanceSpinner() {
493		m.spinnerFrame = spinner.Dot.Frames[m.spinnerIdx%len(spinner.Dot.Frames)]
494		m.spinnerIdx++
495	}
496	
497	// busyLabel returns the action running on an item, and whether there is one.
498	func (m *Model[T]) busyLabel(item T) (string, bool) {
499		if m.cfg.Key == nil || len(m.busy) == 0 {
500			return "", false
501		}
502		label, ok := m.busy[m.cfg.Key(item)]
503		return label, ok
504	}
505	
506	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
507	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
508		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
509		m.rebuild()
510	}
511	
512	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
513	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
514	
515	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
516	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
517		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
518	
519		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
520		for i, item := range m.visible {
521			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
522			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
523				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
524			}
525			rows[i] = cells
526		}
527		m.table.SetRows(rows)
528	
529		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
530		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
531		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
532		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
533		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
534		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
535		case len(rows) == 0:
536			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
537			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
538			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
539			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
540		case cursor >= len(rows):
541			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
542		case cursor < 0:
543			m.table.SetCursor(0)
544		}
545		m.afterCursorMove()
546	}
547	
548	// afterCursorMove is what every cursor, height and item change ends with: the
549	// styles follow the selected item, and the scroll window follows the cursor.
550	// Keeping them on one call is what stops a new call site from remembering one
551	// and forgetting the other — the offset was invisible while bubbles owned it.
552	func (m *Model[T]) afterCursorMove() {
553		m.clampOffset()
554		m.applyStyles()
555	}
556	
557	// applyStyles asks the view for the styles that go with the selected item.
558	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
559		if !m.table.Focused() {
560			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
561		}
562		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
563		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok {
564			if m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
565				styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
566			}
567			// Busy wins over whatever the view asked for, and this is the one place
568			// it can be said: the highlight is applied to the joined row, so a
569			// colour inside it would close with a reset and end the highlight
570			// mid-row (see render.go). An `exited` container being removed is not
571			// exited-and-that-is-that — the state is what the action is about to
572			// change, so the transition is the newer fact.
573			if _, busy := m.busyLabel(item); busy {
574				styles.Selected = theme.TableStylesForState("busy").Selected
575			}
576		}
577		// Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
578		// in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
579		// counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border by
580		// however much the row's icons disagreed. Padding to a width the row can
581		// never exceed is a no-op when they agree.
582		if m.width > 2 {
583			styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2)
584		}
585		m.setStyles(styles)
586	}
587	
588	// setStyles keeps bubbles' copy and this package's in step. The rendering reads
589	// the one here (render.go); bubbles' is still what Table() reports, which the
590	// tests and any view reaching for the raw table expect to be current.
591	func (m *Model[T]) setStyles(styles table.Styles) {
592		m.styles = styles
593		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
594	}
595	
596	// filtered applies the search query and the toggle filters.
597	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
598		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
599		active := m.activeTokens()
600	
601		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
602		for _, item := range m.items {
603			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
604				continue
605			}
606			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
607				continue
608			}
609			out = append(out, item)
610		}
611		return out
612	}
613	
614	func (m *Model[T]) activeTokens() map[string]bool {
615		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
616		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {
617			if m.bar.IsTokenActive(tok.Label) {
618				active[tok.Label] = true
619			}
620		}
621		return active
622	}
623	
624	// matchesQuery tests the query against each searchable column and then against
625	// the row as a whole.
626	//
627	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
628	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
629	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
630	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
631	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
632	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
633		var joined strings.Builder
634		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
635			if c.Search == nil {
636				continue
637			}
638			value := c.Search(item)
639			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
640				return true
641			}
642			if joined.Len() > 0 {
643				joined.WriteByte(' ')
644			}
645			joined.WriteString(value)
646		}
647		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
648	}
649	
650	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
651	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
652	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
653		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
654			return items
655		}
656		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
657		desc := m.sortDesc
658		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
659			if desc {
660				return less(items[j], items[i])
661			}
662			return less(items[i], items[j])
663		})
664		return items
665	}

14	// InEditMode returns true when a modal, filter, or logs viewport is active
15	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
16		return m.confirmModal != nil || m.containerTable.InEditMode() || m.state == stateLogs
17	}
18	
19	// FilterBarVisible returns true when the filter bar is visible (implements app.FilterBarView).
20	func (m Model) FilterBarVisible() bool {
21		return m.containerTable.FilterBar().IsVisible()
22	}
23	
24	// GetFooterHeight returns the footer height for this view (Rule 124).
25	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
26		// filter bar (when visible) + empty line + info line
27		return 2 + m.containerTable.FilterBar().ExtraHeight()
28	}
29	
30	// RenderFooter returns the footer content rendered below the viewport (Rule 124).
31	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
32		var parts []string
33		if bar := m.containerTable.FilterBar(); bar.IsVisible() {
34			parts = append(parts, bar.View())
35		}
36		infoLine := theme.EmptyLineBg(width)
37		switch {
38		case m.errorMsg != "":
39			infoLine = theme.PadWithBg(theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(m.errorMsg), width)
40		case m.actionLine() != "":
41			infoLine = theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg("  ")+
42				lipgloss.NewStyle().
43					Background(theme.ColorBackground).
44					Foreground(theme.ColorHighlight).
45					Render(m.actionLine()), width)
46		}
47		parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), infoLine)
48		return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
49	}
50	
51	// actionLine names what is running, in words. The spinner on the row says that
52	// *something* is; this says what.
53	//
54	// It is rendered from the current state rather than assigned to a footer
55	// message, because a footer message expires after three seconds (Rule 128) and
56	// a `docker stop` outlives that by seven — the same reason §3.17's sync
57	// progress is a rendered line rather than footerInfo.
58	//
59	// An error takes the line ahead of it: a failure the user has not read yet
60	// matters more than the progress of what is still running.
61	func (m Model) actionLine() string {
62		if m.pruning {
63			return "Pruning containers…"
64		}
65		labels := m.containerTable.BusyLabels()
66		switch len(labels) {
67		case 0:
68			return ""
69		case 1:
70			return labels[0] + "…"
71		default:
72			// Naming them all would run past the line on a wide selection; the count
73			// is what the user is waiting on anyway.
74			return fmt.Sprintf("%d actions running…", len(labels))
75		}
76	}

19	// The logs pane used to live here — a viewState, a viewport, soft wrap, ANSI
20	// stripping, scroll keys, reload, follow, a timestamps toggle and an external
21	// pager. None of it was specific to containers except the last three, and those
22	// are properties of where the text came from rather than of the pane, so the
23	// whole thing moved into the document viewer and the three became a Source's
24	// optional capabilities (see sources.go). `l` and `i` now emit one message and
25	// this view goes back to being a table.
26	
27	// Model represents the containers view state
28	type Model struct {
29		config         *config.Config
30		showAll        bool
31		containerTable datatable.Model[docker.Container]
32		spinner        spinner.Model
33		loading        bool
34		errorMsg       string
35		confirmModal   *sharedcomponents.ConfirmModal
36		// pendingAction is the confirm modal's routing key, and only that.
37		//
38		// It used to be two fields in one: the routing key ("confirm-delete",
39		// "confirm-prune") that handleConfirmYes reads, and a sentence for the user
40		// ("Stopping web") that nothing ever rendered. Carrying both is why nobody
41		// noticed the second had no reader — the field was plainly in use. What the
42		// user is told now comes from the table's busy set.
43		pendingAction string
44		// pruning is the one action that belongs to no row: it acts on the whole
45		// list, so marking every row would say something false. It gets a footer
46		// line of its own instead.
47		pruning       bool
48		width, height int
49	}
50	
51	// Messages
52	
53	// RefreshTickMsg triggers periodic refresh
54	type RefreshTickMsg time.Time
55	
56	// ContainersListMsg contains fetched containers
57	type ContainersListMsg struct {
58		Containers []docker.Container
59		Err        error
60	}
61	
62	// ContainerMetricsMsg contains fetched metrics
63	type ContainerMetricsMsg struct {
64		Metrics map[string]docker.Container
65		Err     error
66	}
67	
68	// ContainerActionMsg signals result of a container action (stop, restart, remove).
69	//
70	// ID used to be the container's *name*: every command filled it from its `name`
71	// argument. Nothing caught it because the only reader was a log line, where a
72	// name reads perfectly well. It matters now — the busy marker is keyed on the
73	// ID, so a message carrying a name would never lift it and the row would spin
74	// for the life of the view.
75	type ContainerActionMsg struct {
76		Action string
77		ID     string
78		Name   string
79		Err    error
80	}
81	
82	// ContainerPruneMsg signals result of a container prune operation
83	type ContainerPruneMsg struct {
84		Output string

86	}

88	// PagerExitMsg signals return from a pager (less) or shell process

90		Err error
91	}
92	
93	// ShellWindowOpenedMsg signals the result of launching a shell in a new terminal window
94	type ShellWindowOpenedMsg struct {
95		Err error

98	// columnStatus indexes containerColumns. Only the ones something else refers to

103		columnImage
104	)
